instruction: For each year from 2019 to 2022, locate the Best Long Paper Award recipient in ACL Anthology and enter the title, year, authors (comma-separated), and ACL PDF link into the best_awards_acl.xlsx file on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires recording ACL Best Long Paper Awards for 4 years (2019-2022) with complete data. Evaluator extracts and validates: (1) exactly 4 data rows, (2) years 2019-2022, (3) non-empty paper titles, (4) author names (comma-separated), (5) valid ACL Anthology PDF links. Custom getter extracts all cell data, metric performs comprehensive verification with partial credit scoring.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies all instruction requirements - row count (4), years (2019-2022), non-empty titles, non-empty authors, and valid ACL PDF links
Correct getter logic: Getter extracts year, title, authors, and link from columns 1-4 of the Excel file

Comprehensive metric logic: Metric validates 5 criteria with partial credit scoring - (1) row count = 4, (2) years exactly [2019,2020,2021,2022], (3) all titles non-empty, (4) all authors non-empty, (5) all links contain ACL domain
Proper postconfig: Activates LibreOffice window and saves file (Ctrl+S) before verification to ensure fresh state
Expected values semantically correct: Specifies 4 rows and years 2019-2022 as required by instruction
Minor limitation: Cannot verify actual content accuracy (e.g., correct paper titles/authors) without gold dataset, but this is practically infeasible - evaluator checks structural correctness instead
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor enhancement: Could add check for comma-separated format in authors field (currently only checks non-empty)
Minor enhancement: Could validate URL format more strictly (e.g., starts with 'http' and contains '.pdf'), though current domain check is reasonable
